## Batch label updates

Labels of already-imported samples can be changed in batches. A batch is a
UTF-8 JSON file:

```json
{
  "batch": "renumber-2026-01",
  "changes": [
    {"sha256": "<full SHA-256 digest>", "old": "cat", "new": "kitten"},
    {"sha256": "<full SHA-256 digest>", "old": "dog", "new": null}
  ]
}
```

- `batch` must be a non-empty string.
- `old` is the expected current label; `new` is the target label. Both may
  be a string or `null`; `null` and the empty string both mean *unlabeled*,
  any other string is taken literally (including Chinese text and a class
  named `unlabeled`).
- The whole batch is verified before anything is written: an unknown
  digest, a sample listed twice, a non-string/non-null label, a malformed
  file, or any sample whose current label differs from its expected old
  label rejects the entire batch with the offending record identified.
- Records whose target equals the current label are no-ops; if every
  record is a no-op, the batch reports `no-changes`, occupies no batch
  number and writes no history.

```bash
python3 -m vision_workbench label ./workspace <digest>      # current label
python3 -m vision_workbench find-label ./workspace <label>  # samples of one label
python3 -m vision_workbench batch ./workspace changes.json   # submit a batch
python3 -m vision_workbench history ./workspace              # successful batches
python3 -m vision_workbench undo ./workspace <batch-number>  # undo a batch
```

See [Finding samples by label](#finding-samples-by-label) for the
`find-label` query, including the empty-string query for unlabeled
samples.

Submitting the same number with the same content again returns the
original result without re-modifying anything (list order and the
`null`/`""` spelling do not change the content), even if labels were
changed in the meantime. The same number with different content is a
conflict.

Before either verdict, the submitted number must identify **exactly one
entry** in the full saved history list. When the same batch number
occurs on a second history entry — whether the two sit next to each
other or have other, legitimate batches between them — the whole
submission is refused as corrupted batch history, with the same rule an
undo uses. The two entries' contents never resolve the ambiguity:
byte-for-byte identical entries are a repeat too, and entries touching
different samples, recording different label changes or carrying
different undo states are refused just the same. Submission never picks
the first occurrence, the last, the still-active one or one not yet
undone, and the two entries are never merged, renumbered or
de-duplicated. The refusal comes before the same-content replay and the
different-content conflict (and before the no-change short-circuit), so
matching one entry's content exactly never selects it, and an entry
already marked undone surfaces the ambiguity instead of replaying. The
error names the batch number as submitted and the 1-based positions of
the first and second occurrence in the full history list; with three or
more occurrences the first two positions are named. The command exits
non-zero with nothing on standard output and no traceback, changes no
sample label or label revision, appends no history, and deletes,
renumbers or repairs neither entry. The full list is scanned, so a
restorable first occurrence never masks a repeat later. Numbers are
matched by their saved raw string exactly — surrounding whitespace and
case are never trimmed or folded, so `"b1"`, `"B1"` and `" b1"` are
different numbers. Only the submitted number is judged: a duplicate of
some *other* number neither blocks a new batch number nor reuse of an
intact, uniquely numbered batch, and this check still runs after the
unknown-sample rejection, which keeps its precedence.

Before either verdict, the saved batch with that number is checked for
the same one-row-per-sample integrity an undo relies on: the same full
SHA-256 digest may appear on at most one of its records. Because
same-content comparison is order-insensitive and works on record sets, a
duplicated row would otherwise collapse into the original record and a
repeat of the exact first submission would report `already-applied`
again, counting a single label change twice. A second occurrence — an
exact copy of a record that changed a label, two records carrying
different before/after labels for one digest, or a copy of a record that
never changed a label — is therefore corrupted batch history, never
records to merge or de-duplicate: the digest alone decides, even when
other samples sit between the two occurrences. The whole record list is
scanned, so a unique record at the front never masks a repeat further
back, and the damage is reported even when the repeat content would
otherwise be a number conflict or the batch has already been undone —
never as an ordinary conflict or as a normal replay. The error names the
submitted batch number, the duplicated sample's full SHA-256 digest and
the two 1-based record positions (the first occurrence and the one that
repeats it).

The saved batch is also checked for the same label-field integrity an
undo relies on: every one of its records must explicitly carry both the
before label `old` and the after label `new`. A record missing either
key — distinguished as missing `old`, missing `new`, or missing both —
makes the batch history corrupted, and the whole repeat submission is
refused before it can return the original statistics or report a number
conflict. The command exits non-zero with nothing on standard output and
no traceback, and the error names the submitted batch number, the
offending sample's full SHA-256 digest and the record's 1-based position
inside that batch. Key presence alone decides: an explicitly saved
`null` or empty string is a recorded unlabeled label and still takes
part in same-content comparison, and a real class literally named
`unlabeled` stays its own category; full labels keep their case,
whitespace and Chinese text exactly. Every record is examined,
including unchanged rows and records behind otherwise valid ones, so a
complete record at the front never masks a gap later, and the damage is
reported even when the repeat content would otherwise conflict or the
batch has already been undone. The missing value is never reconstructed
from this submission or from the sample's current label. On either
refusal nothing changes — sample labels, their revisions, the history
records, undo markers and saved split plans stay as they were, no field
is filled in and no new result is appended. Only the batch named by the
submission is inspected: a repeated sample or missing label fields in a
*different* batch neither block a new batch number nor reuse of another
batch's intact history.

The saved batch is likewise checked for the same `changed`-flag
integrity an undo relies on: every record's flag must agree with the
before/after labels saved on that same record. A replay reconstructs
the original statistics from those flags, so a record that saved `cat`
→ `dog` but is flagged unchanged would be replayed as `already-applied`
with the sample miscounted as untouched, and a record flagged changed
on identical before/after labels would inflate the changed count. Both
are corrupted batch history, and the whole repeat submission is refused
before it can return the original statistics or report a number
conflict — never reported as a successful submission, and never
auto-corrected and then accepted. Whether the two labels differ is
judged exactly as the undo judges it: `null` and the empty string spell
the same unlabeled state, so swapping them is not a change, while a
real class literally named `unlabeled` is an ordinary label; every
other label compares as the exact original string, with case, leading
or trailing whitespace, Chinese text and path separators all
significant. The decision uses only the labels stored in the history
record — never the sample's current label and never the labels in this
submission — so a record that recorded `cat` → `dog` but is flagged
unchanged is corruption even if the sample has since been changed back
to `cat`. The command exits non-zero with nothing on standard output
and no traceback, and the error names the submitted batch number, the
sample's full SHA-256 digest, the record's 1-based position inside that
batch and the exact contradiction (a false flag with differing labels,
or a true flag with identical labels). Every record is examined,
including records that recorded no real change and records behind
otherwise valid ones, so a consistent record at the front never masks a
contradiction later, and the damage is reported even when the repeat
content would otherwise conflict or the batch has already been undone.
On refusal nothing changes — sample labels, their revisions, the
history records and undo markers stay as they were, no flag is
rewritten and no new result is appended. Only the batch named by the
submission is inspected: the same contradiction in a *different* batch
neither blocks a new batch number nor reuse of another batch's intact
history.

`history` lists successful batches in submission order: the samples
involved, their before/after labels, and the number of samples actually
changed. Failed batches never enter history.

`undo` restores the old labels of a batch, but only for samples the batch
actually changed and only when none of them was modified afterwards (even
if the label was changed back). Other samples' later changes do not block
the undo. Undo leaves a queryable record; repeating it reports
`already-undone`.

### Corrupted batch history

The number an `undo` names must identify **exactly one batch** in the saved
history list. (Re-submitting a batch number is held to the same rule: see
the number-uniqueness refusal above.) When the same batch number occurs on
a second entry — whether the two entries sit next to each other or have
other, legitimate batches between them — the whole undo is refused as
corrupted batch history. The two entries' contents never resolve the
ambiguity: byte-for-byte identical entries are a repeat too, and entries
touching different samples, recording different label changes or carrying
different undo states are refused just the same. Undo never picks the
first occurrence, the last, the still-active one or one not yet undone,
and the two entries are never merged, renumbered or de-duplicated. The error names the batch number as given and the
1-based positions of the first and second occurrence in the full history
list; with three or more occurrences the first two positions are named. The
command exits non-zero with nothing on standard output and no traceback,
changes no sample label or label revision, rewrites neither the
registration list nor the batch history, sets no undo marker or undo time,
and deletes, renumbers or repairs neither conflicting entry. The full list
is scanned, so a restorable first occurrence never masks a repeat that
appears later, and a first occurrence already marked undone surfaces this
ambiguity instead of returning `already-undone`. Numbers are matched by
their saved raw string exactly — surrounding whitespace and case are never
trimmed or folded, so `"b1"` and `" b1"` are different numbers. Only the
requested number is judged: a duplicate of some *other* number never blocks
a unique, otherwise valid target from undoing normally, and a number absent
from the list still returns the ordinary unknown-batch error.

Every record of the uniquely resolved target batch must name its sample in
the exact identity spelling registration uses: a `sha256` of **exactly 64
lowercase hexadecimal characters**. An empty string, any other length, an
uppercase letter, a non-hexadecimal character, or whitespace before, after
or inside the value makes the batch history corrupted. Such a value is
never repaired — not by trimming the whitespace, folding it to lowercase,
truncating or padding it to 64 characters — and the original identity is
never inferred from the current sample list: even when the rewritten value
would name a registered sample, the record as saved is refused. The whole
record list is examined, including records that did not change a label and
records standing behind otherwise valid ones, and the check finishes before
any sample is restored or an `already-undone` answer is returned, so a
restorable record at the front can never hide a malformed one further back.
The command exits with a non-zero status, prints nothing on standard output
and no traceback, and reports on standard error that the **batch history**
is corrupted — naming the requested batch number, the record's 1-based
position inside that batch, the raw `sha256` value and exactly what is
wrong with its format (empty, wrong length, uppercase/non-hexadecimal
characters, or whitespace). Sample labels and their revisions, the batch
records, the undo marker and saved split plans all stay exactly as they
were. This judges format only, on the one target batch: the same malformed
value in a *different* batch does not stop an intact batch from undoing
normally, a number absent from the history still returns the ordinary
unknown-batch error, and a record whose `sha256` is well formed but names a
sample that has since left the registration list is still handled by the
ordinary missing-sample rule below.

Every sample record stored for a successful batch carries a `rev`: the
sample's label revision at the moment the batch finished, which an undo
pins against. That `rev` is mandatory on **every** history record —
whether the record actually changed a label or not — and must be a genuine
non-negative integer. A boolean (`true`), a decimal (`1.0`), a numeric
string (`"1"`), `null` and a missing field are all invalid; a missing
revision is never treated as zero, and the integer `0` on an unchanged
record stays legal. This requirement is specific to batch history: the
optional `rev` on manifest registrations keeps its old compatibility
behaviour, including records that omit it.

When an undo targets a batch containing such a record, the command exits
with a non-zero status, prints nothing on standard output and no
traceback, and reports on standard error that the **batch history** is
corrupted — naming the batch number, the sample's full SHA-256 digest and
the exact `rev` problem. The whole undo is refused even if an earlier
record in the same batch was restorable: no sample changes label, and
neither the registration list nor the batch history is rewritten,
default-filled or given a new undo marker. This refusal is distinct from
the normal "sample modified after the batch" rejection and from an
unknown batch number — a corrupt record can never be reported as undone,
as having no changes, or as an unknown batch. Corruption is checked before
the repeated-undo short-circuit too, so a batch already marked undone
still surfaces its bad record instead of returning `already-undone`.

A batch history is likewise corrupted when the **same sample content
digest appears on more than one record of the target batch**. Undo is one
restore per sample, pinned by that digest, so a duplicated row — even an
exact copy of a record that genuinely changed a label, or a copy of a
record that did not change one — would otherwise restore one sample
several times, add its label revision repeatedly and overstate the
restored count. Such a batch is never merged or de-duplicated: the whole
undo is refused. The decision is made from the full SHA-256 digest alone,
regardless of the labels, whether the before/after labels differ or
whether the record actually changed anything, so two records with
different label content for one digest are still a duplicate. Every
record in the batch is examined, so a perfectly restorable record at the
front can never hide a repeat that appears later; the error names the
batch number, the duplicated sample's full digest and the two 1-based
record positions (the first occurrence and the one that repeats it). As
with a bad revision, the command exits non-zero with nothing on standard
output and no traceback, changes no sample label or revision, rewrites
neither the registration list nor the batch history, sets no new undo
marker, and is reported even when the batch is already marked undone
rather than as `already-undone`. The later-modification conflict, an
unknown batch number and a successful undo are all distinct from this
refusal.

A batch history is likewise corrupted when a record's **`changed` flag
contradicts the before/after labels saved on that same record**. Undo treats
a flagged-changed row as a sample to restore from `new` back to `old` and to
count, and a flagged-unchanged row as one it never restores, so the flag must
match the record's own stored labels:

- the before and after labels are judged equal when both are unlabeled
  (`null` and the empty string spell the same state, so swapping them is not
  a change), and otherwise compared as the exact original strings — case,
  leading or trailing whitespace, Chinese text and path separators keep
  their meaning, and a real class literally named `unlabeled` is a label and
  never equals the unlabeled state;
- differing before/after labels therefore require `changed: true`, and
  identical labels require `changed: false`.

The decision uses only the labels stored in the history record; it never
substitutes the sample's current label, so a row that recorded `cat` → `dog`
but is flagged unchanged is corruption even if the sample has since been
changed back to `cat`. Such a hidden change would otherwise leave the sample
at `dog` while the batch is recorded as undone, and a false change on
identical labels would count and "restore" a sample the batch never touched.
The whole undo is refused: the error names the batch number, the sample's
full SHA-256 digest, the record's 1-based position inside the target batch
and the exact contradiction (false flag with differing labels, or true flag
with identical labels), with nothing on standard output and no traceback.
Every record in the batch is examined, so a restorable record at the front
is never partially restored first, and nothing is auto-corrected, dropped or
rewritten — no sample label or revision changes, neither the registration
list nor the batch history is rewritten, and no undo marker or undo time is
added. As with the other integrity damage, it is reported even when the
batch is already marked undone rather than as `already-undone`, is distinct
from the later-modification conflict and an unknown batch number, and only
the target batch is examined — the same contradiction in another batch does
not stop a valid batch from undoing normally and restoring exactly the
samples it actually changed.

The same sample participating in two *different* batches over time is
normal and stays legal; only a repeat inside the one target batch is an
error. Damage in a different batch does not matter: only the target batch's
records are examined, so a valid batch still undoes normally.

Imports, batch writes and undos are crash-safe: a write-ahead journal
installs the manifest and the history together, so after an interruption
the workspace shows either the old state or the complete new state with
its history — labels and their history never straddle the two. Recovery
runs under the workspace lock at the start of every operation, so a
process that already has the workspace open also completes a peer's
prepared transaction without reopening; a sample imported successfully
afterwards is never rolled back by that recovery. Concurrent operations
are serialized by the lock, so no successful import or batch is lost and
two batches modifying the same sample from the same old label cannot both
win. Summary, label and history queries each observe one complete state
and never report corruption from an in-flight write. Saved split plans are
never touched by imports, label changes or undos; plans created afterwards
use the current labels, and the same-name reuse/conflict rules still
apply.

1	"""Stratified train/validation/test split planning.
2	
3	A plan allocates every sample to exactly one of three sets.  Exact rational
4	arithmetic (:mod:`fractions`) drives the allocation so that, for every
5	class *and* for the dataset as a whole, each set's sample count differs
6	from its proportional expectation by strictly less than one.
7	
8	Assignments derive solely from sample identities (content digests), labels
9	and the integer seed, so they are independent of import order, manifest
10	ordering, workspace location and process restarts.
11	"""
12	
13	from __future__ import annotations
14	
15	import hashlib
16	import math
17	import re
18	from fractions import Fraction
19	from typing import Any, Sequence
20	
21	# Sentinel for samples without a label.  An object (not the string
22	# "unlabeled") keeps a real class literally named "unlabeled" separate.
23	UNLABELED = object()
24	
25	SET_NAMES = ("train", "validation", "test")
26	
27	# A sample identity is a full SHA-256 digest: exactly 64 lowercase
28	# hexadecimal characters.  The same spelling the registration manifest
29	# enforces is required inside saved split plans, so a truncated digest,
30	# an uppercase spelling, surrounding whitespace or a stray non-hex digit
31	# can never be repaired by truncating, padding, stripping or changing
32	# case.
33	_DIGEST_RE = re.compile(r"[0-9a-f]{64}\Z")
34	
35	
36	class SplitError(ValueError):
37	    """A split parameter or record is invalid."""
38	
39	
40	def invalid_digest_reason(value: Any) -> str | None:
41	    """Return why ``value`` is not a full lowercase SHA-256 digest, else None.
42	
43	    The accepted spelling is exactly 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters,
44	    matching the registered sample identity format.  A non-string value
45	    (including a missing ``None``), an empty string, a digest of any other
46	    length, an uppercase spelling or surrounding whitespace is rejected
47	    with a concrete reason; the value is never normalized into acceptance.
48	    """
49	    if value is None:
50	        return (
51	            "the field is missing or null; expected a string of 64 "
52	            "lowercase hexadecimal characters"
53	        )
54	    if not isinstance(value, str):
55	        return (
56	            f"it is a {type(value).__name__}, not a string; expected a "
57	            "string of 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters"
58	        )
59	    if not value:
60	        return "it is empty; expected 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters"
61	    if value != value.strip() or any(char in " \t\r\n" for char in value):
62	        return (
63	            "it contains surrounding or embedded whitespace; expected 64 "
64	            "lowercase hexadecimal characters without spaces"
65	        )
66	    if len(value) != 64:
67	        return (
68	            f"it has {len(value)} characters instead of 64; expected 64 "
69	            "lowercase hexadecimal characters"
70	        )
71	    if _DIGEST_RE.fullmatch(value) is None:
72	        # Length is exactly 64 here, so every remaining problem is a
73	        # non-hex or uppercase character.
74	        return (
75	            "it must contain only lowercase hexadecimal characters "
76	            "(digits 0-9 and letters a-f)"
77	        )
78	    return None
79	
80	
81	def category_key(label: Any) -> Any:
82	    """Stratum key for a manifest label value.
83	
84	    ``None`` and the empty string both mean "unlabeled", matching
85	    :meth:`DatasetStore.summary`; any other label is taken literally.
86	    """
87	    if label is None or label == "":
88	        return UNLABELED
89	    return label
90	
91	
92	def category_name(key: Any) -> str:
93	    """Render a stratum key for JSON output.
94	
95	    The unlabeled stratum renders as the empty string (which mirrors the
96	    manifest's empty-label meaning); a genuine class literally named
97	    ``"unlabeled"`` therefore stays distinguishable.
98	    """
99	    return "" if key is UNLABELED else str(key)
100	
101	
102	def _sort_key(key: Any) -> tuple[int, str]:
103	    return (0 if key is UNLABELED else 1, category_name(key))
104	
105	
106	def validate_name(name: str) -> str:
107	    if not isinstance(name, str) or not name.strip():
108	        raise SplitError("Split plan name must not be empty or only whitespace")
109	    if "/" in name or "\\" in name:
110	        raise SplitError("Split plan name must not contain '/' or '\\'")
111	    if name in (".", ".."):
112	        raise SplitError("Split plan name must not be '.' or '..'")
113	    return name
114	
115	
116	def parse_ratio(value: Any) -> Fraction:
117	    """Parse one ratio as a finite number in the closed interval [0, 1]."""
118	    if isinstance(value, bool):
119	        raise SplitError(f"Ratio must be a number, got {value!r}")
120	    if isinstance(value, float):
121	        if not math.isfinite(value):
122	            raise SplitError(f"Ratio must be finite, got {value!r}")
123	        # Use the shortest decimal that round-trips, so 0.1 means 1/10
124	        # rather than its binary approximation.
125	        value = repr(value)
126	    try:
127	        if isinstance(value, Fraction):
128	            ratio = value
129	        elif isinstance(value, int):
130	            ratio = Fraction(value)
131	        elif isinstance(value, str):
132	            ratio = Fraction(value)
133	        else:
134	            raise SplitError(f"Ratio must be a number, got {value!r}")
135	    except (ValueError, ZeroDivisionError, ArithmeticError, OverflowError):
136	        raise SplitError(f"Ratio must be a finite number, got {value!r}") from None
137	    if ratio < 0 or ratio > 1:
138	        raise SplitError(
139	            f"Ratio must be between 0 and 1 (inclusive), got {value!r}"
140	        )
141	    return ratio
142	
143	
144	def validate_ratios(ratios: Sequence[Any]) -> tuple[Fraction, Fraction, Fraction]:
145	    if len(ratios) != 3:
146	        raise SplitError("Exactly three ratios (train, validation, test) are required")
147	    parsed = tuple(parse_ratio(value) for value in ratios)
148	    if sum(parsed, Fraction(0)) != 1:
149	        raise SplitError("Ratios must sum to exactly 1")
150	    return parsed  # type: ignore[return-value]
151	
152	
153	def allocation_table(
154	    strata_counts: dict[Any, int], ratios: tuple[Fraction, Fraction, Fraction]
155	) -> dict[Any, tuple[int, int, int]]:
156	    """Allocate integer ``(train, validation, test)`` counts per stratum.
157	
158	    Construction: every cell starts at ``floor(N_c * p_s)``; each stratum
159	    then distributes its leftover free units (at most two per row) and each
160	    column total must land on ``floor`` or ``ceil`` of its own expectation.
161	    A free unit may only enter a non-integral cell.  An integral placement
162	    always exists (controlled rounding of the fractional-parts table); the
163	    small max-flow below searches the deterministic floor/ceil choices.
164	    Every used cell ends at ``floor`` or ``ceil`` of its expectation and
165	    every column total at ``floor``/``ceil`` of its, hence every
166	    discrepancy is strictly below one.
167	    """
168	    strata = sorted(strata_counts, key=_sort_key)
169	    total = sum(strata_counts.values())
170	
171	    floors: dict[Any, list[int]] = {}
172	    parts: dict[Any, list[Fraction]] = {}
173	    for c in strata:
174	        expectation = [Fraction(strata_counts[c]) * ratios[j] for j in range(3)]
175	        floors[c] = [e.numerator // e.denominator for e in expectation]
176	        parts[c] = [e - floors[c][j] for j, e in enumerate(expectation)]
177	
178	    # Fractional column sums S_j; a column receives floor(S_j) or
179	    # ceil(S_j) free units.  sum_j S_j is the integer number of free
180	    # units, so the fractional parts sum to an integer k: exactly k
181	    # non-integral columns round up.  A column whose S_j is integral
182	    # cannot round up (that would be a discrepancy of exactly one), so
183	    # the size-k subsets are tried until a flow matches every row.
184	    column_sums = [sum((parts[c][j] for c in strata), Fraction(0)) for j in range(3)]
185	    column_base = [s.numerator // s.denominator for s in column_sums]
186	    row_supply = {c: int(sum(parts[c])) for c in strata}
187	    extra_needed = sum(row_supply.values()) - sum(column_base)
188	    eligible = [j for j in range(3) if column_sums[j] != column_base[j]]
189	
190	    flows = _controlled_rounding(
191	        strata, parts, row_supply, column_base, extra_needed, eligible
192	    )
193	
194	    table: dict[Any, tuple[int, int, int]] = {}
195	    for c in strata:
196	        table[c] = tuple(floors[c][j] + flows[c][j] for j in range(3))  # type: ignore[assignment]
197	        if sum(table[c]) != strata_counts[c]:
198	            raise SplitError("Internal error: stratum count mismatch")  # pragma: no cover
199	    for j in range(3):
200	        column_total = sum(table[c][j] for c in strata)
201	        expect_total = Fraction(total) * ratios[j]
202	        if abs(Fraction(column_total) - expect_total) >= 1:
203	            raise SplitError("Internal error: total count mismatch")  # pragma: no cover
204	    return table
205	
206	
207	def _controlled_rounding(
208	    strata: Sequence[Any],
209	    parts: dict[Any, list[Fraction]],
210	    row_supply: dict[Any, int],
211	    column_base: list[int],
212	    extra_needed: int,
213	    eligible: Sequence[int],
214	) -> dict[Any, list[int]]:
215	    """Place every row's free units on non-integral cells.
216	
217	    Column j receives ``column_base[j]`` units, plus one for each member
218	    of a size-``extra_needed`` subset of eligible columns (its total then
219	    rounds ``S_j`` to floor or ceil).  Candidate subsets are tried in a
220	    fixed order; the fractional parts themselves prove the rounded
221	    polytope has an integral vertex, so one candidate always yields a
222	    full-value flow.
223	    """
224	    from itertools import combinations
225	
226	    if extra_needed == 0:
227	        candidates: list[tuple[int, ...]] = [()]
228	    else:
229	        candidates = list(combinations(eligible, extra_needed))
230	
231	    last_error: Exception | None = None
232	    for extra in candidates:
233	        demand = column_base[:]
234	        for j in extra:
235	            demand[j] += 1
236	        try:
237	            return _integral_flow(strata, parts, row_supply, demand)
238	        except SplitError as error:  # candidate infeasible, try next
239	            last_error = error
240	    raise SplitError(
241	        f"Internal error: cannot satisfy split proportions: {last_error}"
242	    )  # pragma: no cover
243	
244	
245	def _integral_flow(
246	    strata: Sequence[Any],
247	    parts: dict[Any, list[Fraction]],
248	    row_supply: dict[Any, int],
249	    column_demand: list[int],
250	) -> dict[Any, list[int]]:
251	    """Max-flow placement; raises unless every free unit is placed."""
252	    source = ("s",)
253	    sink = ("t",)
254	    row_nodes = [("r", i) for i in range(len(strata))]
255	    col_nodes = [("c", j) for j in range(3)]
256	    residual: dict[Any, dict[Any, int]] = {source: {}, sink: {}}
257	    for node in row_nodes + col_nodes:
258	        residual[node] = {}
259	
260	    def add_edge(u: Any, v: Any, capacity: int) -> None:
261	        residual[u][v] = capacity
262	        residual[v].setdefault(u, 0)
263	
264	    required = 0
265	    for i, c in enumerate(strata):
266	        supply = row_supply[c]
267	        required += supply
268	        if supply:
269	            add_edge(source, row_nodes[i], supply)
270	        for j in sorted(range(3), key=lambda k: (-parts[c][k], k)):
271	            if parts[c][j] > 0:
272	                add_edge(row_nodes[i], col_nodes[j], 1)
273	    for j, node in enumerate(col_nodes):
274	        add_edge(node, sink, column_demand[j])
275	
276	    pushed = 0
277	    while pushed < required:
278	        path = _augmenting_path(residual, source, sink, row_nodes, col_nodes)
279	        if path is None:
280	            raise SplitError("no feasible integral placement")
281	        for u, v in zip(path, path[1:]):
282	            residual[u][v] -= 1
283	            residual[v][u] += 1
284	        pushed += 1
285	
286	    flows = {c: [0, 0, 0] for c in strata}
287	    for i, c in enumerate(strata):
288	        for j, col in enumerate(col_nodes):
289	            # Forward edge capacity was 1; residual reverse flow of 1
290	            # means the unit was placed in this cell.
291	            flows[c][j] = residual[col].get(row_nodes[i], 0)
292	    return flows
293	
294	
295	def _augmenting_path(
296	    residual: dict[Any, dict[Any, int]],
297	    source: Any,
298	    sink: Any,
299	    row_nodes: Sequence[Any],
300	    col_nodes: Sequence[Any],
301	) -> list[Any] | None:
302	    """Breadth-first augmenting path with fixed node traversal order."""
303	    order = [source, *row_nodes, *col_nodes, sink]
304	    previous: dict[Any, Any] = {source: None}
305	    queue = [source]
306	    head = 0
307	    while head < len(queue):
308	        node = queue[head]
309	        head += 1
310	        for neighbor in order:
311	            if neighbor in previous:
312	                continue
313	            if residual.get(node, {}).get(neighbor, 0) > 0:
314	                previous[neighbor] = node
315	                if neighbor == sink:
316	                    path = [sink]
317	                    while path[-1] is not source:
318	                        path.append(previous[path[-1]])
319	                    path.reverse()
320	                    return path
321	                queue.append(neighbor)
322	    return None
323	
324	
325	def seeded_order(digests: Sequence[str], seed: int) -> list[str]:
326	    """Deterministic seed-driven order of the given digests.
327	
328	    Each digest gets a sort key ``H(seed || digest)`` from SHA-256, with
329	    the digest itself breaking ties.  Unlike :mod:`random`, this stream is
330	    defined by the hash algorithm itself, so it is stable across Python
331	    versions and only depends on the digest set and the seed.
332	    """
333	    seed_bytes = str(seed).encode("utf-8")
334	    return sorted(
335	        digests,
336	        key=lambda digest: (
337	            hashlib.sha256(seed_bytes + digest.encode("utf-8")).digest(),
338	            digest,
339	        ),
340	    )
341	
342	
343	def assign(samples: Sequence[dict[str, Any]], ratios: Sequence[Any], seed: Any) -> dict[str, str]:
344	    """Return ``{digest: set_name}`` for the given manifest-like samples.
345	
346	    Each sample mapping must contain ``sha256`` and ``label`` keys.
347	    """
348	    if isinstance(seed, bool) or not isinstance(seed, int):
349	        raise SplitError(f"Seed must be an integer, got {seed!r}")
350	    ratio_values = validate_ratios(ratios)
351	
352	    digests: list[str] = []
353	    seen: set[str] = set()
354	    strata_counts: dict[Any, int] = {}
355	    stratum_of: dict[str, Any] = {}
356	    for sample in samples:
357	        if not isinstance(sample, dict):
358	            raise SplitError("Every sample record must be an object")
359	        digest = sample.get("sha256")
360	        if not isinstance(digest, str) or not digest:
361	            raise SplitError("Every sample needs a non-empty 'sha256' identity")
362	        if digest in seen:
363	            raise SplitError(f"Duplicate sample identity in manifest: {digest}")
364	        seen.add(digest)
365	        key = category_key(sample.get("label"))
366	        stratum_of[digest] = key
367	        strata_counts[key] = strata_counts.get(key, 0) + 1
368	        digests.append(digest)
369	
370	    table = allocation_table(strata_counts, ratio_values)
371	    positions = {digest: i for i, digest in enumerate(seeded_order(digests, seed))}
372	
373	    assignment: dict[str, str] = {}
374	    for key, row in table.items():
375	        members = sorted(
376	            (d for d in digests if stratum_of[d] == key),
377	            key=lambda d: positions[d],
378	        )
379	        start = 0
380	        for j, count in enumerate(row):
381	            for digest in members[start : start + count]:
382	                assignment[digest] = SET_NAMES[j]
383	            start += count
384	    return assignment
385

1	"""Strict validation of the on-disk sample registration manifest.
2	
3	Every feature that uses the current manifest — summary, label queries,
4	batch updates, imports and plan creation — validates the *whole*
5	registration list before touching any sample.  A manifest is usable only
6	when it is an object whose ``schema_version`` is the integer ``1`` and
7	whose ``items`` is a list of complete, well-typed sample records with no
8	repeated digest.  Booleans and decimals never stand in for integers
9	(``True == 1`` in Python), numeric strings never stand in for sizes, and
10	duplicate registrations are reported rather than merged or silently
11	resolved to one copy.
12	"""
13	
14	from __future__ import annotations
15	
16	import re
17	from typing import Any
18	
19	MANIFEST_SCHEMA_VERSION = 1
20	
21	# A full SHA-256 digest: exactly 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters.
22	_DIGEST_RE = re.compile(r"[0-9a-f]{64}\Z")
23	
24	
25	class ManifestError(ValueError):
26	    """The registration manifest is structurally unusable."""
27	
28	
29	def _is_integer(value: Any) -> bool:
30	    """Whether ``value`` is a genuine integer.
31	
32	    Booleans are rejected even though ``bool`` subclasses ``int`` (so
33	    ``True`` cannot masquerade as version ``1`` or as a byte size), and
34	    every other non-integer type (floats, including integral ones such as
35	    ``1.0``, numeric strings, ``None``) is rejected as well.
36	    """
37	    return isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool)
38	
39	
40	def validate_manifest(data: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
41	    """Validate a parsed manifest payload and return it unchanged.
42	
43	    Structural problems describe the offending part; a bad sample record
44	    names its 1-based position in the list and the offending field; a
45	    digest registered twice names the digest and both record positions.
46	    The whole list is checked, so valid records preceding a bad one never
47	    mask a later error.
48	    """
49	    if not isinstance(data, dict):
50	        raise ManifestError(
51	            "Dataset manifest is corrupted: manifest must be a JSON object"
52	        )
53	    version = data.get("schema_version")
54	    if not _is_integer(version):
55	        raise ManifestError(
56	            "Dataset manifest is corrupted: schema_version must be the integer 1"
57	        )
58	    if version != MANIFEST_SCHEMA_VERSION:
59	        raise ManifestError(
60	            f"Dataset manifest is corrupted: unsupported schema version {version}"
61	        )
62	    items = data.get("items")
63	    if not isinstance(items, list):
64	        raise ManifestError(
65	            "Dataset manifest is corrupted: items must be a JSON array of samples"
66	        )
67	
68	    seen: dict[str, int] = {}
69	    for position, item in enumerate(items, start=1):
70	        location = f"sample #{position}"
71	        if not isinstance(item, dict):
72	            raise ManifestError(
73	                f"Dataset manifest is corrupted: {location} must be a JSON object"
74	            )
75	
76	        digest = item.get("sha256")
77	        if not isinstance(digest, str):
78	            raise ManifestError(
79	                f"Dataset manifest is corrupted: {location} is missing its "
80	                "string 'sha256' field"
81	            )
82	        if not _DIGEST_RE.fullmatch(digest):
83	            raise ManifestError(
84	                f"Dataset manifest is corrupted: {location} has an invalid "
85	                f"'sha256' field {digest!r}: expected 64 lowercase hexadecimal "
86	                "characters"
87	            )
88	
89	        if "source" not in item:
90	            raise ManifestError(
91	                f"Dataset manifest is corrupted: {location} (sha256 {digest}) "
92	                "is missing its non-empty string 'source' field"
93	            )
94	        source = item["source"]
95	        if not isinstance(source, str):
96	            raise ManifestError(
97	                f"Dataset manifest is corrupted: {location} (sha256 {digest}) "
98	                "has an invalid 'source' field: expected a non-empty string"
99	            )
100	        if not source:
101	            raise ManifestError(
102	                f"Dataset manifest is corrupted: {location} (sha256 {digest}) "

1	"""Batch label-update submission, validation and history.
2	
3	A batch file is a UTF-8 JSON object of the form::
4	
5	    {
6	      "batch": "non-empty batch number",
7	      "changes": [
8	        {"sha256": "<full SHA-256 digest>", "old": <string or null>,
9	         "new": <string or null>}
10	      ]
11	    }
12	
13	``null`` and the empty string both mean "unlabeled"; any other string is
14	taken literally (including Chinese text and a class named ``unlabeled``).
15	"""
16	
17	from __future__ import annotations
18	
19	import re
20	from dataclasses import dataclass
21	from typing import Any, Callable, Iterator, Mapping, Sequence
22	
23	BATCH_SCHEMA_VERSION = 1
24	
25	# A registered sample identity is a full SHA-256 digest: exactly 64
26	# lowercase hexadecimal characters — the same spelling the registration
27	# manifest enforces.  Undo requires every target-batch record to pin a
28	# sample in that exact spelling, so a truncated or padded digest, an
29	# uppercase spelling, surrounding or embedded whitespace or any other
30	# non-hex character can never be accepted by stripping, lowercasing,
31	# truncating or padding.
32	_DIGEST_RE = re.compile(r"[0-9a-f]{64}\Z")
33	
34	
35	@dataclass(frozen=True)
36	class BatchResolution:
37	    """One record's verdict, produced before anything is written.
38	
39	    ``current`` is the label read once during verification and ``changed``
40	    is whether ``new`` differs from it.  A resolution never references the
41	    manifest item or its revision, so the decision stays independent of
42	    the later workspace save.
43	    """
44	
45	    sha256: str
46	    old: str | None
47	    new: str | None
48	    current: str | None
49	    changed: bool
50	
51	
52	class BatchError(ValueError):
53	    """A batch submission or undo request is invalid."""
54	
55	
56	def normalize_label(label: Any) -> str | None:
57	    """Map the two unlabeled spellings to ``None``; keep strings literal.
58	
59	    Raises :class:`BatchError` for anything that is not a string or ``None``.
60	    """
61	    if label is None or label == "":
62	        return None
63	    if isinstance(label, str):
64	        return label
65	    raise BatchError(f"label must be a string or null, got {label!r}")
66	
67	
68	def render_label(label: str | None) -> str:
69	    """Human-readable rendering for messages."""
70	    return "unlabeled" if label is None else label
71	
72	
73	def parse_batch_file(data: Any) -> tuple[str, list[dict[str, Any]]]:
74	    """Validate a parsed batch payload; return ``(number, records)``.
75	
76	    Each record is ``{"sha256": str, "old": str | None, "new": str | None}``
77	    with labels normalized (``None`` for unlabeled).  Structural problems,
78	    an empty batch number and duplicate digests are all rejected here.
79	    """
80	    if not isinstance(data, dict):
81	        raise BatchError("batch file must contain a JSON object")
82	    number = data.get("batch")
83	    if not isinstance(number, str) or not number.strip():
84	        raise BatchError("batch number must be a non-empty string")
85	    changes = data.get("changes")
86	    if not isinstance(changes, list):
87	        raise BatchError("batch file must contain a 'changes' list")
88	
89	    records: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
90	    seen: set[str] = set()
91	    for index, change in enumerate(changes):
92	        location = f"change #{index + 1}"
93	        if not isinstance(change, dict):
94	            raise BatchError(
95	                f"{location}: must be an object with 'sha256', 'old' and 'new'"
96	            )
97	        if not all(key in change for key in ("sha256", "old", "new")):
98	            raise BatchError(
99	                f"{location}: must contain 'sha256', 'old' and 'new' keys"
100	            )
101	        digest = change["sha256"]
102	        if not isinstance(digest, str) or not digest:
103	            raise BatchError(f"{location}: 'sha256' must be a non-empty string")
104	        if digest in seen:
105	            raise BatchError(f"{location}: duplicate sample {digest}")
106	        seen.add(digest)
107	        old = normalize_label(change["old"])
108	        new = normalize_label(change["new"])
109	        records.append({"sha256": digest, "old": old, "new": new})
110	    return number, records
111	
112	
113	def content_key(records: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> frozenset[tuple[str, str | None, str | None]]:
114	    """Order- and spelling-insensitive identity of a batch's content.
115	
116	    Two submissions with the same number are considered the same batch
117	    when their record sets compare equal here: list order does not matter
118	    and ``null`` vs ``""`` does not matter.  Labels are normalized on both
119	    sides before comparing, so the equality also holds across the two
120	    places records come from — freshly parsed records (already normalized
121	    to ``None``) and history rows loaded from disk, which may have legally
122	    saved either unlabeled spelling.  Every other string is kept exactly,
123	    so a real class named ``unlabeled`` never matches an unlabeled record
124	    and case, surrounding whitespace, Chinese text and path separators
125	    stay significant.
126	    """
127	    return frozenset(
128	        (
129	            record["sha256"],
130	            normalize_label(record["old"]),
131	            normalize_label(record["new"]),
132	        )
133	        for record in records
134	    )
135	
136	
137	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
138	# Submission rules
139	#
140	# Each stage is a pure function of parsed records and the state passed to
141	# it; none of them mutate the manifest or the history.  The stages line up
142	# with the conditions that reject a submission, in their original order:
143	#
144	#   1. reject_unknown_samples  — records naming no registered sample
145	#   2. resolve_re_submission   — same-number history: the number must
146	#                                identify one entry in the full history
147	#                                list (require_unique_history_number
148	#                                refusal), the existing entry must list
149	#                                each sample once (corruption refusal),
150	#                                save both labels on every record
151	#                                (corruption refusal) and carry a changed
152	#                                flag that matches those labels
153	#                                (corruption refusal), then replay or
154	#                                conflict
155	#   3. verify_records          — one current-label pass: old-label
156	#                                mismatches reject the whole batch; the
157	#                                surviving resolutions also decide which
158	#                                records actually change
159	#   4. apply_resolutions       — the only mutating stage (store layer)
160	#   5. build_history_entry / result_payload — result/history assembly
161	#
162	# "Current label" is read exactly once for the whole submission (stage 3),
163	# so verification and the change decision never process it twice.
164	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
165	
166	# A current-label lookup: full digest -> normalized current label (or
167	# ``None`` when the digest names no registered sample).
168	CurrentLabels = Callable[[str], str | None]
169	
170	
171	def reject_unknown_samples(
172	    records: list[dict[str, Any]], known: Callable[[str], bool]
173	) -> None:
174	    """Reject the batch if any record names a sample that is not registered.
175	
176	    The first unknown record is reported, in submission order.
177	    """
178	    for record in records:
179	        if not known(record["sha256"]):
180	            raise BatchError(f"sample not found: {record['sha256']}")
181	
182	
183	def resolve_re_submission(
184	    number: str,
185	    records: list[dict[str, Any]],
186	    existing: dict[str, Any] | None,
187	) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
188	    """Handle a batch number already present in history.
189	
190	    Equal content (per :func:`content_key`) replays the first submission's
191	    result without touching the manifest — even when samples have since
192	    changed — while different content conflicts.  Returns the replay
193	    result, or ``None`` when the number is free.
194	
195	    Integrity is refused before either verdict.  The same-number entry
196	    must list every sample at most once (see
197	    :func:`require_intact_history_records`): a content digest appearing on
198	    a second record is batch-history corruption, and it has to be caught
199	    here because :func:`content_key` compares record *sets*, so a
200	    duplicated row would otherwise collapse away and the replay would
201	    count the sample's label change twice.  The entry must also
202	    explicitly carry both ``old`` and ``new`` on every record first (see
203	    :func:`require_intact_history_labels`): a row missing either key is
204	    corruption too, never an unlabeled label to guess, and it is reported
205	    before the replay or the conflict verdict — an entry that would
206	    otherwise conflict is refused for the damage instead.  Explicitly
207	    saved ``null`` and ``""`` stay ordinary unlabeled labels and take
208	    part in the comparison as usual.  Finally, every record's ``changed``
209	    flag must agree with the before/after labels saved on that same
210	    record (see :func:`require_intact_history_changes`): a replay
211	    reconstructs the original statistics from those flags, so a row
212	    flagged unchanged while its labels differ would silently swallow a
213	    real change, and a row flagged changed on identical labels would
214	    inflate the changed count — both are corruption, judged from the
215	    stored labels alone, never from the sample's current label or this
216	    submission's labels.
217	    """
218	    if existing is None:
219	        return None
220	    require_intact_history_records(existing)
221	    require_intact_history_labels(existing)
222	    require_intact_history_changes(existing)
223	    if content_key(existing["records"]) == content_key(records):
224	        return replay_result(existing)
225	    raise BatchError(
226	        f"batch number {number!r} is already used with different content"
227	    )
228	
229	
230	def verify_records(
231	    records: list[dict[str, Any]], current_label: CurrentLabels
232	) -> list[BatchResolution]:
233	    """Verify every expected old label and classify each record, in one pass.
234	
235	    Each record's current label is looked up once and used for both
236	    decisions: a current label differing from the expected old rejects the
237	    whole batch; otherwise the record is classified as changed only when
238	    the target label differs from that same current label.  No manifest
239	    item is modified here.
240	    """
241	    resolutions: list[BatchResolution] = []
242	    for record in records:
243	        current = current_label(record["sha256"])
244	        if current != record["old"]:
245	            raise BatchError(
246	                f"change for {record['sha256']}: expected old label "
247	                f"{render_label(record['old'])!r} but current label is "
248	                f"{render_label(current)!r}"
249	            )
250	        resolutions.append(
251	            BatchResolution(
252	                sha256=record["sha256"],
253	                old=record["old"],
254	                new=record["new"],
255	                current=current,
256	                changed=current != record["new"],
257	            )
258	        )
259	    return resolutions
260	
261	
262	def apply_resolutions(
263	    resolutions: list[BatchResolution],
264	    items: Mapping[str, dict[str, Any]],
265	) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
266	    """Mutate manifest items for the resolved records and build history rows.
267	
268	    This is the only stage that changes samples: records flagged
269	    ``changed`` receive their target label and a new revision; no-op
270	    records keep both.  Every row additionally records the revision after
271	    the batch, which later undos pin against.  The pre-change revision is
272	    read from each item here, once, rather than during verification.
273	    """
274	    applied: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
275	    for resolution in resolutions:
276	        item = items[resolution.sha256]
277	        revision = item_revision(item)
278	        if resolution.changed:
279	            item["label"] = resolution.new
280	            revision += 1
281	            item["rev"] = revision
282	        applied.append(
283	            {
284	                "sha256": resolution.sha256,
285	                "old": resolution.old,
286	                "new": resolution.new,
287	                "changed": resolution.changed,
288	                "rev": revision,
289	            }
290	        )
291	    return applied
292	
293	
294	def build_history_entry(
295	    number: str, applied_records: list[dict[str, Any]]
296	) -> dict[str, Any]:
297	    """Assemble the history row for a batch with at least one change."""
298	    return {
299	        "batch": number,
300	        "records": applied_records,
301	        "changed_count": sum(1 for record in applied_records if record["changed"]),
302	        "undone": False,
303	        "undone_at": None,
304	    }
305	
306	
307	def result_payload(
308	    number: str, status: str, applied_records: list[dict[str, Any]]
309	) -> dict[str, Any]:
310	    """Build the user-facing result, keeping the original count meanings.
311	
312	    ``changed`` counts records that actually changed a label,
313	    ``unchanged`` counts target-equals-current records and ``total``
314	    counts every submitted record.
315	    """
316	    changed = sum(1 for record in applied_records if record["changed"])
317	    return {
318	        "batch": number,
319	        "status": status,
320	        "changed": changed,
321	        "unchanged": len(applied_records) - changed,
322	        "total": len(applied_records),
323	    }
324	
325	
326	def no_changes_result(number: str, total: int) -> dict[str, Any]:
327	    """Result for a batch whose records all match their current labels."""
328	    return {
329	        "batch": number,
330	        "status": "no-changes",
331	        "changed": 0,
332	        "unchanged": total,
333	        "total": total,
334	    }
335	
336	
337	def replay_result(entry: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
338	    """Reconstruct the original result from a stored history entry."""
339	    return result_payload(entry["batch"], "already-applied", entry["records"])
340	
341	
342	def item_revision(item: dict[str, Any]) -> int:
343	    """Read a sample's label revision, treating malformed stored values as 0."""
344	    value = item.get("rev", 0)
345	    return value if isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool) else 0
346	
347	
348	def describe_history_revision_problem(value: Any, *, present: bool) -> str | None:
349	    """Describe why a history record's ``rev`` is not a usable revision.
350	
351	    Every batch-history sample record must carry ``rev`` as a genuine
352	    non-negative integer: the revision pinned for later undos.  Booleans
353	    (``True == 1``), decimals (``1.0 == 1``), numeric strings (``"1"``),
354	    ``null`` and a missing field are all rejected rather than coerced, so
355	    they can never compare equal to a sample's current revision.  Returns
356	    ``None`` when the value is valid.
357	    """
358	    if not present:
359	        return "missing 'rev' field"
360	    if isinstance(value, bool):
361	        return f"'rev' must be a non-negative integer, got boolean {value!r}"
362	    if not isinstance(value, int):
363	        return f"'rev' must be a non-negative integer, got {value!r}"
364	    if value < 0:
365	        return f"'rev' must be a non-negative integer, got negative {value}"
366	    return None
367	
368	
369	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
370	# History integrity checks
371	#
372	# Every ``require_intact_history_*`` check scans the same record list of
373	# the same target batch entry, so the shared mechanics live in two
374	# helpers: ``_iter_history_records`` reads the list once, rejects a
375	# missing list or a non-object row and yields ``(position, record)``
376	# pairs; ``_corruption_prefix`` and ``_record_ref`` assemble the common
377	# "Batch history is corrupted: batch ..." message parts.  The checks
378	# themselves stay separate passes and keep their original order on the
379	# undo path — digest formats, then duplicate digests, then revisions,
380	# then labels, then changed flags — each reporting its first problem in
381	# record order.  Re-submission (``resolve_re_submission``) reuses only
382	# the three checks that verdict needs, in the same order: duplicate
383	# digests, then labels, then changed flags, all running before the
384	# same-content replay / different-content conflict decision.  Those are per-entry checks; the
385	# coarser ``require_unique_history_number`` check — that the submitted
386	# number identifies one entry at all in the full history list — is
387	# shared with undo and runs on the submit path even earlier, before the
388	# entry is selected (see ``find_unique_history_entry`` below).
389	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
390	
391	
392	def _corruption_prefix(entry: Mapping[str, Any]) -> str:
393	    """Shared prefix of every batch-history corruption message."""
394	    return f"Batch history is corrupted: batch {entry.get('batch')!r}"
395	
396	
397	def _record_ref(record: Mapping[str, Any], position: int | None = None) -> str:
398	    """Locate a history record by sample digest and optional 1-based position."""
399	    ref = f"sample {record.get('sha256')}"
400	    if position is not None:
401	        ref += f", record #{position}"
402	    return ref
403	
404	
405	def _iter_history_records(
406	    entry: Mapping[str, Any],
407	) -> Iterator[tuple[int, Mapping[str, Any]]]:
408	    """Yield ``(position, record)`` for each row of a batch history entry.
409	
410	    This is the shared front half of every integrity check: the entry
411	    must carry a record list and every row must be an object.  Positions
412	    are 1-based, matching the record numbers used in error messages.
413	    """
414	    prefix = _corruption_prefix(entry)
415	    records = entry.get("records")
416	    if not isinstance(records, list):
417	        # validate_history() already rules this out; defend direct callers.
418	        raise BatchError(f"{prefix}: missing records")
419	    for position, record in enumerate(records, start=1):
420	        if not isinstance(record, dict):
421	            raise BatchError(f"{prefix}: malformed record")
422	        yield position, record
423	
424	
425	def describe_history_digest_problem(value: Any) -> str | None:
426	    """Describe why a history record's ``sha256`` is not a registered identity.
427	
428	    Every sample undo pins must be named in the exact spelling used at
429	    registration: a string of exactly 64 lowercase hexadecimal
430	    characters.  An empty string, any other length, uppercase letters,
431	    non-hex characters and surrounding or embedded whitespace are all
432	    rejected with a concrete reason; the value is never normalized into
433	    acceptance by stripping whitespace, folding case, truncating or
434	    padding, and no identity is inferred from the current sample list.
435	    Returns ``None`` when the value is well formed.
436	    """
437	    if not isinstance(value, str):
438	        # validate_history() already rules a missing or non-string
439	        # digest out; defend direct callers just the same.
440	        return (
441	            "it is not a string; expected a string of 64 lowercase "
442	            "hexadecimal characters"
443	        )
444	    if not value:
445	        return "it is empty; expected 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters"
446	    if value != value.strip() or any(char in " \t\r\n" for char in value):
447	        return (
448	            "it contains surrounding or embedded whitespace; expected 64 "
449	            "lowercase hexadecimal characters without spaces"
450	        )
451	    if len(value) != 64:
452	        return (
453	            f"it has {len(value)} characters instead of 64; expected 64 "
454	            "lowercase hexadecimal characters"
455	        )
456	    if _DIGEST_RE.fullmatch(value) is None:
457	        # Length is exactly 64 here, so what remains is an uppercase
458	        # letter or a non-hexadecimal character.
459	        return (
460	            "it must contain only lowercase hexadecimal characters "
461	            "(digits 0-9 and letters a-f)"
462	        )
463	    return None
464	
465	
466	def require_intact_history_digests(entry: Mapping[str, Any]) -> None:
467	    """Reject a batch entry whose records do not pin registered identities.
468	
469	    Undo restores and counts samples purely from the target batch's
470	    history rows, so every row's ``sha256`` must name a sample in the
471	    exact spelling registration uses: a string of exactly 64 lowercase
472	    hexadecimal characters.  An empty string, a digest of any other
473	    length, an uppercase spelling, a non-hexadecimal character or
474	    surrounding or embedded whitespace is batch-history corruption —
475	    never a value to strip, lowercase, truncate or pad into acceptance,
476	    and never an identity to guess from the samples currently
477	    registered: even a spelling whose normalized form would name a known
478	    sample is refused as saved.  Whether the record actually changed a
479	    label is irrelevant; its position in the record list is irrelevant
480	    too.  The error names the batch number, the record's 1-based
481	    position inside the target batch, the raw saved ``sha256`` value and
482	    the exact format problem; nothing is repaired, rewritten or restored.
483	
484	    The whole record list is scanned in order — unchanged rows and rows
485	    behind restorable ones included — so a well-formed row at the front
486	    can never mask a malformed one further back, and no sample is
487	    restored before the damage is found.  This judges format only, not
488	    registration: a well-formed digest of a sample that has since left
489	    the manifest is left to undo's ordinary missing-sample rule.
490	
491	    Callers must run this before any success-shaped short-circuit (such
492	    as an already-undone batch), so corruption can never be masked by a
493	    repeated-undo success.
494	    """
495	    for position, record in _iter_history_records(entry):
496	        problem = describe_history_digest_problem(record.get("sha256"))
497	        if problem is not None:
498	            raise BatchError(
499	                f"{_corruption_prefix(entry)}, "
500	                f"{_record_ref(record, position)}: invalid 'sha256' value "
501	                f"{record.get('sha256')!r}: {problem}"
502	            )
503	
504	
505	def require_intact_history_records(entry: Mapping[str, Any]) -> None:
506	    """Reject a batch entry whose records are not one row per sample.
507	
508	    Undo pins every stored record to a sample content digest, so a digest
509	    may occur at most once in the target batch: a duplicated row — even a
510	    byte-for-byte copy, or a copy of a record that never changed a label —
511	    would otherwise restore the same sample more than once, bump its label
512	    revision repeatedly and inflate the restored count.  Duplicates are
513	    therefore batch-history corruption, never records to merge or
514	    de-duplicate.  The decision is independent of the labels, the
515	    before/after labels and the record's ``changed`` flag: the content
516	    digest alone decides.
517	
518	    The whole record list is scanned, so rows preceding the repeat are
519	    checked too and a restorable row at the front can never mask a later
520	    duplicate.  On a repeat the error names the batch number, the sample's
521	    full digest and both 1-based record positions; nothing is repaired.
522	
523	    Callers must run this before any success-shaped short-circuit (such as
524	    an already-undone batch or a same-number replay), so corruption can
525	    never be masked by a repeated-undo success or by a replay whose
526	    set-based content comparison would collapse the duplicate into one.
527	    """
528	    seen: dict[str, int] = {}
529	    for position, record in _iter_history_records(entry):
530	        digest = record.get("sha256")
531	        if digest in seen:
532	            raise BatchError(
533	                f"{_corruption_prefix(entry)}, sample {digest} "
534	                f"appears more than once, at record #{seen[digest]} and "
535	                f"record #{position}"
536	            )
537	        seen[digest] = position
538

540	def require_intact_history_revisions(entry: Mapping[str, Any]) -> None:
541	    """Reject a batch entry whose records lack a sound pinned ``rev``.
542	
543	    Every record — changed or not — must carry ``rev`` as a genuine
544	    non-negative integer, since undo pins each changed sample to the
545	    revision it had at the end of the batch.  This is integrity damage,
546	    unlike the *manifest's* optional revision (see
547	    :func:`item_revision`, which keeps the legacy missing-means-zero
548	    behaviour): a bad row is reported with the batch number, the sample's
549	    full digest and the exact ``rev`` problem, and nothing is repaired.
550	
551	    Callers must run this before any success-shaped short-circuit (such as
552	    an already-undone batch), so corruption can never be masked by a
553	    repeated-undo success.
554	    """
555	    for _position, record in _iter_history_records(entry):
556	        problem = describe_history_revision_problem(
557	            record.get("rev"), present="rev" in record
558	        )
559	        if problem is not None:
560	            raise BatchError(
561	                f"{_corruption_prefix(entry)}, "
562	                f"{_record_ref(record)}: {problem}"
563	            )
564	
565	
566	def describe_missing_history_labels(record: Mapping[str, Any]) -> str | None:
567	    """Describe which of a history record's before/after labels are absent.
568	
569	    Every batch-history sample record must spell out both ``old`` (the
570	    label before the batch) and ``new`` (the label after it).  Only key
571	    presence is judged here: an explicitly saved ``null`` or empty string
572	    is a recorded unlabeled label, never a missing field.  Returns
573	    ``None`` when both keys are present.
574	    """
575	    missing = [key for key in ("old", "new") if key not in record]
576	    if not missing:
577	        return None
578	    if len(missing) == 2:
579	        return "missing 'old' and 'new' labels"
580	    return f"missing {missing[0]!r} label"
581	
582	
583	def require_intact_history_labels(entry: Mapping[str, Any]) -> None:
584	    """Reject a batch entry whose records lack a saved before/after label.
585	
586	    Undo restores and counts samples purely from what the target batch's
587	    history rows say: a changed row is restored from ``new`` back to
588	    ``old``, an unchanged row is left alone.  That is only meaningful
589	    when every row explicitly carries both labels, so a row missing
590	    ``old``, ``new`` or both is batch-history corruption — never an
591	    unlabeled-to-unlabeled no-op to skip, and never something to guess
592	    from the sample's current label.  The error names the batch number,
593	    the sample's full SHA-256 digest, the record's 1-based position
594	    inside the target batch and which of ``old``/``new`` (or both) is
595	    absent; nothing is repaired, rewritten or restored.
596	
597	    An explicitly saved ``null`` or empty string stays legal: both mean
598	    unlabeled, as does a literal class named ``unlabeled`` stay an
599	    ordinary label.  Only a missing key is damage.
600	
601	    The whole record list is scanned in order — unchanged rows and rows
602	    behind restorable ones included — so a complete row at the front can
603	    never mask a damaged one further back, and no sample is restored
604	    before the damage is found.
605	
606	    Callers must run this before any success-shaped short-circuit (such
607	    as an already-undone batch or a same-number replay), so corruption
608	    can never be masked by a success verdict or swallowed by a conflict.
609	    """
610	    for position, record in _iter_history_records(entry):
611	        problem = describe_missing_history_labels(record)
612	        if problem is not None:
613	            raise BatchError(
614	                f"{_corruption_prefix(entry)}, "
615	                f"{_record_ref(record, position)}: {problem}"
616	            )

618	
619	def history_labels_equal(old: Any, new: Any) -> bool:
620	    """Whether two stored history labels describe the same category.
621	
622	    The decision uses the labels saved in the history record itself, never
623	    a sample's current label: ``null`` and the empty string both mean
624	    unlabeled and are therefore equal, while every other value is compared
625	    as the exact original string — case, surrounding whitespace, Chinese
626	    text and path separators all keep their meaning, and a real class
627	    literally named ``unlabeled`` never equals unlabeled.
628	    """

630	
631	
632	def describe_history_change_problem(record: Mapping[str, Any]) -> str | None:
633	    """Describe why a history record's ``changed`` flag contradicts old/new.
634	
635	    The flag must agree with the before/after labels saved on that same
636	    record: differing labels require ``changed: true`` and equal labels
637	    require ``changed: false``.  Returns ``None`` when the flag is
638	    consistent.  The stored labels are validated upstream as strings or
639	    ``None`` and the flag as a boolean, so no type guessing happens here.
640	    """
641	    actually_changed = not history_labels_equal(record["old"], record["new"])
642	    old_label = normalize_label(record["old"])
643	    new_label = normalize_label(record["new"])
644	    if actually_changed and not record["changed"]:
645	        return (
646	            f"'changed' is false but the before/after labels differ: "
647	            f"{render_label(old_label)!r} -> {render_label(new_label)!r}"
648	        )
649	    if not actually_changed and record["changed"]:
650	        return (
651	            f"'changed' is true but the before/after labels are identical: "
652	            f"{render_label(old_label)!r}"
653	        )
654	    return None
655	
656	
657	def require_intact_history_changes(entry: Mapping[str, Any]) -> None:
658	    """Reject a batch entry whose ``changed`` flags belie old/new labels.
659	
660	    Undo restores a sample based on what the history row says the batch
661	    did: a row marked changed is restored from ``new`` back to ``old`` and
662	    counted, while a row marked unchanged is never restored.  So the flag
663	    must match the before/after labels saved on that row — judging from the
664	    record's own stored labels rather than any sample's current label:
665	
666	    * differing old/new (``null`` and ``""`` being the same unlabeled
667	      spelling) require ``changed: true``;
668	    * identical old/new require ``changed: false``.
669	
670	    A row that claims a change with identical labels would make undo count
671	    and restore a sample the batch never touched; a row that hides a real
672	    change would leave the sample at its post-batch label while the batch
673	    is recorded undone.  Both are batch-history corruption: the error names
674	    the batch number, the sample's full SHA-256 digest and the record's
675	    1-based position inside the target batch, together with the exact
676	    contradiction, and nothing is repaired.
677	
678	    The whole record list is scanned in order, so a restorable row at the
679	    front can never mask a contradiction further back.
680	
681	    Callers must run this before any success-shaped short-circuit (such as
682	    an already-undone batch or a same-number replay), so corruption can
683	    never be masked by a repeated-undo success or by a replay whose stored
684	    flags would miscount the original batch.
685	    """
686	    for position, record in _iter_history_records(entry):
687	        problem = describe_history_change_problem(record)
688	        if problem is not None:
689	            raise BatchError(
690	                f"{_corruption_prefix(entry)}, "
691	                f"{_record_ref(record, position)}: {problem}"
692	            )
693	
694	
695	def history_number_positions(
696	    number: str, batches: Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]]
697	) -> list[int]:
698	    """1-based positions of every history entry whose number is ``number``.
699	
700	    Matching is on the batch number's saved raw string — no trimming of
701	    surrounding whitespace and no case folding — so ``"b1"``, ``"B1"``
702	    and ``" b1"`` never meet.  The whole list is scanned rather than
703	    stopping at the first hit, since callers must tell a unique number
704	    from a repeated one.
705	    """
706	    return [
707	        position
708	        for position, entry in enumerate(batches, start=1)
709	        if isinstance(entry, Mapping) and entry.get("batch") == number
710	    ]
711	
712	
713	def require_unique_history_number(
714	    number: str, batches: Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]]
715	) -> None:
716	    """Reject a number appearing on at least two full-history entries.
717	
718	    Both re-submission and undo must resolve a batch number to exactly
719	    one history entry.  A second entry carrying the same number makes the
720	    number ambiguous no matter what the two entries contain — identical
721	    record content, different samples, different label changes or
722	    differing undo states are all refusal, never a reason to pick the
723	    first, the last or the still-active one, and never something to
724	    merge, renumber or de-duplicate.  Whether the entries sit next to
725	    each other or have other batches between them is irrelevant.
726	
727	    On a repeat the error names the user-given batch number and the two
728	    1-based positions of the first and second occurrence in the full
729	    history list; with three or more occurrences only the first two are
730	    named.  Nothing is repaired.  Callers must run this before any
731	    same-number verdict (a same-content replay or a different-content
732	    conflict) and before the already-undone short-circuit: the entries'
733	    content and undo state can never disambiguate the number, and an
734	    entry already marked undone leaves it just as ambiguous.
735	    """
736	    positions = history_number_positions(number, batches)
737	    if len(positions) >= 2:
738	        raise BatchError(
739	            "Batch history is corrupted: batch number "
740	            f"{number!r} appears more than once, at batch #{positions[0]} "
741	            f"and batch #{positions[1]}"
742	        )
743	
744	
745	def find_unique_history_entry(
746	    number: str, batches: Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]]
747	) -> Mapping[str, Any] | None:
748	    """Find the single history entry whose number is ``number``.
749	
750	    An undo target must name exactly one batch.  Matching is on the batch
751	    number's saved raw string — no trimming of surrounding whitespace and
752	    no case folding — so the whole list is scanned with exact equality
753	    rather than stopping at the first hit: a second entry carrying the
754	    same number, whether adjacent to the first or separated by other
755	    batches, makes the target ambiguous.  Such a history is corrupted no
756	    matter what the two entries contain — identical record content,
757	    different samples, different label changes or differing undo states
758	    are all refusal, never a reason to pick the first, the last or the
759	    still-active one, and never something to merge.
760	
761	    Returns the unique entry, or ``None`` when the number does not occur.
762	    On a repeat the error names the user-given batch number and the two
763	    1-based positions of the conflicting entries in the full history
764	    list, so neither record is undone, preferred or repaired.  Callers
765	    must run this before every per-entry integrity check and before the

769	    positions = history_number_positions(number, batches)

773	    # disagree; the positions are already known to number at least one.
774	    require_unique_history_number(number, batches)
775	    return batches[positions[0] - 1]
776

778	def empty_history() -> dict[str, Any]:
779	    return {"schema_version": BATCH_SCHEMA_VERSION, "batches": []}

784	    if not isinstance(data, dict) or data.get("schema_version") != BATCH_SCHEMA_VERSION:
